title: The two-particle density matrix of a Luttinger liquid
authors: Harini Radhakrishnan, Matthias Thamm, Hatem Barghathi, Bernd Rosenow, Adrian Del Maestro
abstract: Two-particle coherence is the first level of the reduced-density-matrix hierarchy that contains correlations inaccessible to single-particle observables, yet analytic two-particle density matrices are rare even in one dimension. We derive a closed, finite-size expression for the equal-time two-particle reduced density matrix of spinless fermions in a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid using constructive bosonization with an explicit ultraviolet cutoff. In addition to the familiar Luttinger parameter $K$-dependent exponent $γ^2=(K+K^{-1}-2)/2$ which governs the spatial decay of matrix elements, the result exposes a second exponent, $λ=(K^{-1}-K)/2$, which encodes correlations between opposite chiralities and controls the off-diagonal structure. The diagonal limit of the two-particle reduced density matrix yields density correlations and the static structure factor, while its coherences resolve algebraic $2k_F$ charge-density-wave correlations for repulsion and odd-parity p-wave pairing correlations for attraction. After fixing the cutoff from the one-particle density matrix, the analytic result quantitatively reproduces density matrix renormalization group calculations of the interacting J-V chain within the Luttinger liquid regime. The result connects universal Luttinger liquid scaling with observables in finite microscopic systems.
summary: This paper derives a closed-form expression for the two-particle reduced density matrix ($ho_2$) of spinless fermions in a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid. By using constructive bosonization, the authors reveal a second correlation exponent $\lambda$ that governs off-diagonal coherence beyond what single-particle measurements can capture. The result successfully connects universal Luttinger liquid scaling theory with quantitative predictions for finite microscopic systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is deriving an explicit, analytically controlled expression for the equal-time two-particle reduced density matrix ($ho_2$) in strongly correlated 1D systems.
main_result: The authors derive a closed form for $ho_2$ showing two characteristic exponents: one familiar exponent $\gamma_2$ and a new exponent $\lambda$, which controls off-diagonal correlations between opposite chiralities.
method: The calculation employs constructive bosonization techniques combined with the introduction of an explicit ultraviolet cutoff to manage divergences inherent in calculating higher-order correlation functions.
model_or_system: The system studied is spinless fermions modeled as a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) on a ring, which is analyzed using continuum field theory methods derived from the fermionic Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Two-particle reduced density matrix ($ho_2$), pair distribution function ($g_2$), static structure factor, and specific correlation signatures like $2k_F$ charge-density-wave correlations.
important_parameters: The Luttinger parameter $K$, the interaction strength parameters (J/V ratio), and the derived exponents $\gamma_2 = (K+K^{-1}-2)/2$ and $\lambda = (K^{-1}-K)/2$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on bosonization, assuming the system is in the Luttinger liquid regime, and requires fixing the cutoff based on results from the one-particle density matrix.
figures_summary: Figure 1 graphically illustrates $ho_2$ for a 1D N-body system. Figure 2 visualizes $ho_2$ on a spherical surface in $(r, r', \Delta R)$ space, particularly highlighting correlation structures for attractive interactions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds the theory by first introducing the general formalism of reduced density matrices ($ho_n$), then applying constructive bosonization to derive the TLL result, followed by detailed analysis of the resulting correlations, and finally validating the analytic result against numerical DMRG calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides an exact analytical tool (the 2-RDM) for quantifying complex many-body correlations in 1D systems, connecting universal field theory results to measurable quantities in finite microscopic models, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Graphical depiction of the two-body density of a one dimensional N-body system of length L with wavefunc- tion Ψ(x1, . . . xN). The quantity ρ2(x′ 2, x′ 1; x1, x2) denotes the matrix element obtained when two fermions are annihilated at sites x1 and x2 while two are created at coordinates x′ 1 and x′ 2. For periodic boundary conditions, d(L|x′ 2, x1) is the chord length across the ring.

FIG. 2. The 2-RDM ρ2(x′ 2, x′ 1; x1, x2) plotted on the surface of a sphere with ∆R2 + r2/2 + r′2/2 = 144, L = 40, K = 8/5 (attractive), n0 = 1/2, and ϵ = 1 (see Section IV for parame- ter details). The colormap corresponds to a range from −0.03 (blue) to 0.03 (green). Alternating blue-green regions signal the sign change from fermion antisymmetry, while the van- ishing of ρ2 along r = 0, r′ = 0 is due to the Pauli exclusion principle.

FIG. 3. Dependence of the two interaction-dependent expo- nents in the correlation function, γ2 and λ, on the Luttinger parameter K. γ2 is non-negative, while λ, the new exponent in this work, can attain negative values.
FIG. 4. The density-density correlation function g2(r) at fixed L = 50 for different values of the Luttinger parameter K.

FIG. 5. The 2-RDM of the Luttinger model on a ring for attractive K = 8/5, (top row) and repulsive K = 5/8 (bottom row) at two fixed values of ∆R = L/5 + 1/2 (left column) and ∆R = L/5 (right column) where L = 40. The values of ∆R are chosen to suppress (enhance) the first oscillating fermionic term in Eq. (34) as indicated in the panel titles. Red dashed lines denote the lines corresponding to the limits (hyperplanes) x′ 1 →x1, x′ 2 →x2, x′ 2 →x1, and x′ 1 →x2.
